meta.title: {name} – an open source reporting solution
meta.description: Free software to collect KPIs across your organisation, with the evidence behind each figure. Totals are calculated at every level. Templates for the voluntary standard VS and the revised ESRS are included. The auditor checks everything in the tool.

hero.title: An open source reporting solution
hero.lead: {name} is a web tool for collecting KPIs across your sites and subsidiaries. Each figure can be justified with attached evidence. Your data is aggregated through your organisation levels, and accessible to auditors. The software is free: you run it on your own server, or a provider runs it for you.

free.provideTitle: You pay for your own hosting
provide: On one of your company's servers, or with a hosting service that runs it for you (Clever Cloud). Your IT team installs the updates, or lets the server install them at night.

items.a: Yes. There is no paid version. The source code is public, under the AGPL-3.0-or-later licence. You still pay for the hosting.
Try it on your computer, install it on a server with one command, or use managed hosting with Clever Cloud. The Get {name} page helps you choose, and gives the commands and the links.
On one of your company's servers, installed by your IT team. Or with a hosting service that runs it for you (Clever Cloud). Backups run automatically in both cases.

items.q: Do we have to give up Excel?
items.a: No. You still import values from Excel or CSV files. You still export your tables to Excel.

items.q: Does {name} have templates for the ESRS?
items.a: Yes. The library has eleven templates for the revised ESRS of the CSRD (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1563): ESRS 2, E1 to E5, S1 to S4, G1. They are collection templates built from the text of the regulation. Install ESRS 2 and the templates of your material topics, then adapt the KPIs to your company. A KPI shared by several templates is entered once. The KPI texts of these templates are in English and French.

items.q: Does {name} make us compliant with a regulation?
items.a: No, not by itself. It helps you collect the quantitative data you need, for example for the voluntary standard VS, for your ESRS metrics, for gender pay gap reporting.
No. It collects the data and applies the formulas you set. It is not certified carbon accounting software.
No. The data entry page tells them what is left to do, on a computer or a phone.
Every value, with its evidence and its history. They cannot change anything.

Yes, if an administrator has allowed it. The feature is off by default. Each person connects their own assistant with a personal token. The assistant has the same rights as that person. When company sign-in is on, a person who cannot sign in with a password cannot use an assistant.

items.q: Can people sign in with their company account?
items.a: Yes, if you turn it on: it is off by default. It works with Microsoft Entra ID, Google, Okta, Keycloak and the other services that follow the OpenID Connect standard. A space manager turns it on for the whole installation. Then only the space managers keep a password, as rescue accounts. The company account only proves who the person is: the administrators still create the accounts and give the roles in the tool.

items.q: What does IT need to do?
items.a: Install the tool and host it. There is nothing to develop. After the installation with one command, the server also installs the updates at night, unless you turn this off. The IT documentation starts with a list of what to prepare and a security overview.
